correctness.rationale: For any two selected K_n edges, a disjoint pair of unselected edges can meet both, whether the selected edges meet or not. For three selected edges, the only failing type is P4: its two diagonally crossing witnesses are disjoint and meet all three selected edges. A triangle or 3K2 leaves nothing; a star or P3 plus K2 leaves only edges through a single common point. There are 12 forbidden triples per four-set. Deleting one selected edge leaves either an adjacent pair (2(n-3) P4 extensions) or a disjoint pair (4 extensions); subtracting these from the Johnson degrees gives every table entry. Independently checked the universal upper bound by a different reduction from the frozen partition program: any pair uses at most 12 endpoint labels, so embed in K12 and relabel the first triple to one of four type representatives. Directly testing the original isolation condition gave 39,820 K12 states; for each representative and each such target (159,280 pairs), testing for a direct edge, common neighbor, or adjacent first/last neighbors inside the union gave a path of at most three. Since paths only use edges of that union, they pull back to every original n, including n<12. Two disjoint states in K5 force three steps, and the nonisometry witness has all four potential Johnson intermediates forbidden. The independently written check also reproduced the example state and edge counts at n=5,6,7,8.
residual_risks: The general upper-bound proof is a finite exhaustive certificate, not a symbolic exchange lemma. No statement for token slides or KG(n,k) with k>2 is verified.
